question: The arms Act which disallowed Indians from having arms was passed in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1878.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Arms Act, 1878 was enacted by the British colonial government to restrict Indian subjects from possessing, manufacturing, or carrying firearms without a licence. (शस्त्र अधिनियम — 1878)

 

• It was enacted during the viceroyalty of Lord Lytton, in the aftermath of the 1857 revolt, to prevent Indians from arming themselves against British rule.

 

• Notably, the Act exempted Europeans and Anglo-Indians from its licensing requirements, making it explicitly discriminatory against Indians.

 

• The Act was strongly criticised by Indian nationalists, including Surendranath Banerjee, and remained in force (in amended form) for a long period, later evolving into the Arms Act, 1959 after independence.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The same period (Lord Lytton's viceroyalty) also saw the Vernacular Press Act, 1878, which restricted the freedom of the Indian-language press.

 

• Lord Lytton also organised the Delhi Durbar of 1877 proclaiming Queen Victoria as Empress of India.

 

NOTE

 

• 1925 (Option 2): This year is associated with the Kakori Conspiracy, not the Arms Act.

 

• 1920 (Option 3): This year saw the launch of the Non-Cooperation Movement, not the Arms Act.

 

• 1855 (Option 4): This predates the Arms Act; it falls before the 1857 revolt that prompted the legislation.

question: Roquefortine C is found in:
solution_text:
The correct answer is cheese.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Roquefortine C is a mycotoxin (a toxic secondary metabolite) produced by the mould Penicillium roqueforti, which is used to ripen blue cheeses. (रोक्वेफोर्टिन सी — पनीर/चीज़)

 

• It is commonly found in blue-veined cheeses such as Roquefort, Gorgonzola, and Stilton, since these cheeses are made using Penicillium roqueforti cultures.

 

• Roquefortine C is one of several mycotoxins studied for food safety in fermented dairy products, alongside compounds like PR toxin.

 

• Penicillium roqueforti gives blue cheese its characteristic blue-green veining and sharp flavour.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Penicillium is also the genus from which Alexander Fleming discovered the antibiotic Penicillin (from Penicillium notatum).

 

• Other well-known mould-ripened cheeses include Camembert and Brie, made using Penicillium camemberti.

 

NOTE

 

• Meat (Option 1): Roquefortine C is not a characteristic compound of meat products.

 

• Chicken (Option 2): It is not associated with poultry products.

 

• Egg (Option 3): It is not associated with eggs; it is specific to mould-ripened dairy products.

question: The Mohiniyattam dance form originated from which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form that originated in the state of Kerala. (मोहिनीअट्टम — केरल)

 

• The name means "dance of the enchantress" (Mohini), referring to the enchanting female form of Lord Vishnu.

 

• It is a solo dance performed by women, characterised by graceful, swaying body movements, and is considered a Lasya (feminine, graceful) style of dance.

 

• It is one of the eight classical dance forms of India recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, alongside Kathakali (also from Kerala).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Vaishnava Padavali and themes from Vaishnavism form the core repertoire of Mohiniyattam performances.

 

• The dance was revived and popularised in the 20th century largely due to the efforts of poet Vallathol Narayana Menon, founder of the Kerala Kalamandalam.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 2): Karnataka's classical dance form is Yakshagana.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 3): Tamil Nadu's classical dance form is Bharatanatyam.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 4): Maharashtra is known for the folk form Lavani, not a classical dance form of Indian origin like Mohiniyattam.

question: The body of the ______ is circular in cross-section, hence, the name roundworms. They may be free living, aquatic and terrestrial or parasitic in plants and animals.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aschelminthes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Aschelminthes (also called Nematoda or roundworms) are pseudocoelomate animals whose body is circular (cylindrical) in cross-section, giving them the name "roundworms". (एस्केल्मिन्थीज़/निमेटोडा — गोलकृमि)

 

• They may be free-living (found in soil, water) or parasitic in plants and animals, e.g. Ascaris (roundworm), Wuchereria (filarial worm), and Ancylostoma (hookworm).

 

• Unlike flatworms, roundworms have an organ-system level of organisation with a complete alimentary canal (mouth to anus) and are triploblastic, pseudocoelomate, and bilaterally symmetrical.

 

• The body cavity present is a pseudocoelom (a false body cavity not fully lined by mesoderm), distinguishing them from true coelomates.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common human parasitic roundworms include Ascaris lumbricoides (intestinal roundworm) and Enterobius vermicularis (pinworm).

 

• The phylum is also referred to as Nemathelminthes in some classifications.

 

NOTE

 

• Platyhelminthes (Option 1): These are flatworms (e.g. tapeworm, liver fluke) — their bodies are dorsoventrally flattened, not circular in cross-section.

 

• Ctenophores (Option 2): These are marine "comb jellies", radially symmetrical, unrelated to roundworms.

 

• Mollusca (Option 3): This phylum includes soft-bodied animals like snails and octopuses, typically with a shell, not circular worm-like bodies.

question: Which French chemist was one of the first scientists to synthesise organic compounds such as formic acid, methane and acetylene from their elements?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Marcellin Berthelot.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Marcellin Berthelot (1827-1907) was a French chemist celebrated for his pioneering work in total synthesis of organic compounds from their constituent elements. (मार्सेलिन बर्थेलॉट — कार्बनिक रसायन संश्लेषण)

 

• He successfully synthesised compounds such as methane, acetylene, benzene, and formic acid in the laboratory, disproving the earlier notion of "vital force" needed to create organic compounds.

 

• His work helped establish synthetic organic chemistry as a discipline and demonstrated that organic compounds could be created from inorganic starting materials.

 

• He is also known for his contributions to thermochemistry, coining terms such as "exothermic" and "endothermic".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Friedrich Wöhler, a German chemist, is separately famous for synthesising urea from ammonium cyanate in 1828, an earlier landmark in overturning vitalism.

 

• Berthelot also served as a French minister and contributed to explosives research (thermochemistry of explosives).

 

NOTE

 

• Jacob (Jöns Jacob) Berzelius (Option 1): A Swedish chemist known for determining atomic weights and developing chemical notation/symbols, not organic synthesis.

 

• Auguste Laurent (Option 2): A French chemist known for his substitution theory and nucleus theory in organic chemistry, not primarily for total synthesis from elements.

 

• Antoine Lavoisier (Option 4): A French chemist known as the "father of modern chemistry", famous for the law of conservation of mass and disproving phlogiston theory, not organic synthesis.

question: For which year was Manna Dey honored with the Dadasaheb Phalke Award?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2007.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Legendary playback singer Manna Dey was honoured with the Dadasaheb Phalke Award, India's highest award in cinema, for the year 2007. (मन्ना डे — दादासाहेब फाल्के पुरस्कार 2007)

 

• The Dadasaheb Phalke Award is conferred annually by the Government of India (Ministry of Information and Broadcasting) for outstanding contribution to Indian cinema.

 

• It is named after Dhundiraj Govind Phalke, known as Dadasaheb Phalke, the "Father of Indian Cinema", who made India's first full-length feature film, Raja Harishchandra (1913).

 

• Manna Dey was renowned for his versatile playback singing across genres, including classical-based songs, and sang in multiple Indian languages over a career spanning decades.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first Dadasaheb Phalke Award was conferred in 1969 to actress Devika Rani.

 

• The award consists of a Swarna Kamal (Golden Lotus) medallion, a cash prize, and a shawl.

 

NOTE

 

• 2015 (Option 1): The Dadasaheb Phalke Award for that period was given to actor Manoj Kumar (announced 2015).

 

• 2019 (Option 2): This year's award was given to actor Rajinikanth.

 

• 2001 (Option 4): This year's award was given to filmmaker Yash Chopra, not Manna Dey.

question: Ugadi is celebrated in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Andhra Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ugadi is celebrated as the New Year festival in the state of Andhra Pradesh (also in Telangana and, as "Yugadi", in Karnataka). (उगादी — आंध्र प्रदेश)

 

• The word "Ugadi" is derived from the Sanskrit words "Yuga" (age) and "Adi" (beginning), meaning the "beginning of a new age/era".

 

• It marks the first day of the Chaitra month according to the Hindu lunisolar calendar and typically falls in March-April.

 

• A special dish called "Ugadi Pachadi", made with six different tastes (sweet, sour, salty, bitter, spicy and tangy), is prepared to symbolise the varied experiences of life.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The same day is celebrated as Gudi Padwa in Maharashtra and Cheti Chand by the Sindhi community.

 

• In Karnataka, the festival is called Yugadi, celebrated in a similar manner with Bevu-Bella (neem and jaggery).

 

NOTE

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 1): Ugadi is not a traditional festival of Madhya Pradesh.

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 3): Himachal Pradesh's notable local festivals include Kullu Dussehra, not Ugadi.

 

• Kerala (Option 4): Kerala celebrates its New Year as Vishu, not Ugadi.

question: Who has been appointed as the Chief Executive Officer of NITI Aayog in June 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Parameswaran Iyer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Parameswaran Iyer, a retired IAS officer, was appointed as the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of NITI Aayog in June 2022. (परमेश्वरन अय्यर — नीति आयोग सीईओ)

 

• He succeeded Amitabh Kant, who had served as NITI Aayog CEO since 2016 and retired after an extended tenure.

 

• Parameswaran Iyer previously served as the Secretary of the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, where he spearheaded the Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin).

 

• The CEO of NITI Aayog is appointed by the Prime Minister and holds the rank of Secretary to the Government of India, serving a fixed tenure.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) was set up in 2015, replacing the Planning Commission.

 

• The Prime Minister is the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog; the CEO is a fixed-tenure appointment, distinct from the Vice-Chairperson (currently a part-time, non-civil-service position).

 

NOTE

 

• Avinash Kulkarni (Option 1): Not associated with the CEO post of NITI Aayog.

 

• Krishna Srinivasan (Option 2): An economist associated with the IMF (Asia and Pacific Department), not NITI Aayog CEO.

 

• Vivek Kumar (Option 3): Not associated with the CEO post of NITI Aayog.

question: Which special knowledge or practical experience is NOT a condition for being nominated to Rajya Sabha by the President of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Eloquence.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 80 of the Constitution, the President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha who have special knowledge or practical experience in Literature, Science, Art, and Social Service. (राज्यसभा नामांकन — अनुच्छेद 80)

 

• "Eloquence" is not one of the four categories mentioned in Article 80 — it is not a qualifying ground for presidential nomination to the Rajya Sabha.

 

• The purpose of these nominations is to bring eminent persons with domain expertise, who may not otherwise contest elections, into Parliament.

 

• Well-known nominated members over the years have included figures distinguished in these four fields, such as scientists, artists, writers, and social workers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rajya Sabha (Council of States) has a maximum strength of 250 members, with 12 nominated by the President and the rest elected by State/UT legislative assemblies.

 

• Nominated members can vote in presidential elections is a common point of confusion — actually, they cannot vote in the election of the President, but can vote in the election of the Vice-President.

 

NOTE

 

• Science (Option 1): This IS one of the four valid grounds under Article 80.

 

• Art (Option 2): This IS one of the four valid grounds under Article 80.

 

• Literature (Option 4): This IS one of the four valid grounds under Article 80.

question: Achievement of self-reliance and removal of poverty were twin objectives of which five-year plan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fifth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-1979) had the twin objectives of "removal of poverty" (Garibi Hatao) and "attainment of self-reliance". (पंचवर्षीय योजना — पांचवीं योजना)

 

• The plan was formulated by the D.P. Dhar committee and gave the slogan "Garibi Hatao", popularised earlier during Indira Gandhi's 1971 election campaign.

 

• The Fifth Plan also introduced the Minimum Needs Programme (MNP) and emphasised on employment generation and social justice.

 

• The plan was terminated one year early (in 1978) by the Janata Party government, which came to power after the Emergency, and replaced with a rolling plan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-74) had the objectives of "growth with stability" and progress towards self-reliance.

 

• The Third Five-Year Plan (1961-66) aimed to make the economy self-reliant and self-generating, but is more famously remembered for its failure due to the Indo-China (1962) and Indo-Pak (1965) wars and droughts.

 

NOTE

 

• Third (Option 1): Its stated aim was a self-reliant economy, but it is not associated with the specific twin slogan of "self-reliance and removal of poverty" as the Fifth Plan is.

 

• Fourth (Option 3): Its objective was "growth with stability", not the poverty-removal/self-reliance twin objective.

 

• Second (Option 4): The Second Plan (1956-61), based on the Mahalanobis model, focused on rapid industrialisation, especially heavy industries.

question:
Who said the following words?

“Sarfaroshi ki tamanna ab hamare dil me hai, dekhna hai zor kitna baazu-e-qaatil me hai”
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ramprasad Bismil.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The famous revolutionary couplet "Sarfaroshi ki tamanna ab hamare dil me hai..." ("the desire for sacrifice is now in our hearts") is popularly attributed to Ramprasad Bismil, who made it the anthem of the Indian revolutionary movement. (सरफ़रोशी की तमन्ना — रामप्रसाद बिस्मिल)

 

• Ramprasad Bismil was a key figure of the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) and one of the main organisers of the Kakori Conspiracy (1925).

 

• He recited this couplet frequently at revolutionary gatherings, and it became closely associated with his name and legacy, and was later also recited by Bhagat Singh.

 

• Bismil was executed by the British in 1927 at Gorakhpur Jail for his role in the Kakori Conspiracy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The original poet who wrote the couplet is often credited as Bismil Azimabadi, an Urdu poet from Patna, though Ramprasad Bismil is the one who popularised it as a revolutionary slogan.

 

• Ramprasad Bismil also wrote the autobiography "Mera Jeevan Sangharsh".

 

NOTE

 

• Bhagat Singh (Option 2): He famously recited this couplet before his execution, but he is not credited as its original speaker/populariser in the standard convention.

 

• Ras Bihari Bose (Option 3): A revolutionary associated with the Ghadar Movement and the Indian National Army, not linked to this couplet.

 

• Subhash Chandra Bose (Option 4): Leader of the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj), known for the slogan "Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom", not this couplet.

question: Which of the following pairs of countries will host the 2023 FIFA Women’s World Cup?
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Zealand and Australia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2023 FIFA Women's World Cup was jointly hosted by Australia and New Zealand. (फीफा महिला विश्व कप 2023 — ऑस्ट्रेलिया और न्यूज़ीलैंड)

 

• It was the first FIFA Women's World Cup to be hosted by two confederations (Australia from the AFC and New Zealand from the OFC) and the first in the Southern Hemisphere.

 

• The tournament was also the first edition with an expanded 32-team format, up from 24 teams in previous editions.

 

• The tournament was won by Spain, defeating England in the final.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2019 FIFA Women's World Cup was hosted by France and won by the United States.

 

• The next (2027) FIFA Women's World Cup is scheduled to be hosted by Brazil.

 

NOTE

 

• Canada and Mexico (Option 1): Not the host of the 2023 Women's World Cup; Canada and Mexico (along with the USA) are set to co-host the 2026 Men's FIFA World Cup (USA, Canada, Mexico).

 

• New Zealand and Austria (Option 2): Incorrect pairing — the second host was Australia, not Austria.

 

• France and Canada (Option 3): Neither country hosted the 2023 edition; France hosted the 2019 edition alone.

question: Which force is responsible for the motion of the moon around earth?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Centripetal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The centripetal force — provided here by the gravitational force of attraction between the Earth and the Moon — keeps the Moon moving in its (approximately circular) orbit around the Earth. (अभिकेंद्रीय बल — गुरुत्वाकर्षण)

 

• A centripetal force is a force that acts on a body moving in a circular path, directed towards the centre of the circle, and is essential to keep the body from moving off in a straight line (as per Newton's first law).

 

• Without this inward gravitational pull acting as the centripetal force, the Moon would move away from the Earth in a straight line due to inertia.

 

• The magnitude of this force is given by F = mv²/r, where m is mass, v is orbital speed, and r is the orbital radius.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Centrifugal force is a pseudo (fictitious) force that appears to act outward on a body in circular motion, only when observed from a rotating (non-inertial) reference frame.

 

• Other examples of centripetal force in nature include electrons orbiting a nucleus (electrostatic force) and planets orbiting the sun (gravitational force).

 

NOTE

 

• Van der Waals (Option 1): A weak intermolecular force of attraction between molecules, unrelated to orbital motion.

 

• Centrifugal (Option 2): This is the fictitious outward-acting reaction, not the actual force causing the orbital motion.

 

• Frictional (Option 3): Friction is a contact force opposing relative motion between surfaces; it plays no role in the Moon's orbital motion around the Earth (which occurs in a near-vacuum).

question: Who took oath as the 49th Chief Justice of India in August 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uday Umesh Lalit.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Justice Uday Umesh Lalit (U.U. Lalit) took oath as the 49th Chief Justice of India on 27 August 2022. (उदय उमेश ललित — 49वें मुख्य न्यायाधीश)

 

• He succeeded Justice N.V. Ramana as CJI and served a relatively short tenure, retiring on 8 November 2022, before being succeeded by Justice D.Y. Chandrachud.

 

• Justice Lalit was notably elevated directly from the Bar to the Supreme Court bench in 2014, being only the second such direct appointee in Indian judicial history.

 

• The Chief Justice of India is appointed by the President of India under Article 124 of the Constitution, conventionally on the basis of seniority.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Justice Lalit was part of the bench that delivered the landmark judgment declaring the practice of "triple talaq" unconstitutional in 2017.

 

• Justice D.Y. Chandrachud succeeded U.U. Lalit and became the 50th Chief Justice of India in November 2022.

 

NOTE

 

• Sanjiv Kapoor (Option 1): Not a Chief Justice of India; not associated with this appointment.

 

• Ajay Kumar Sood (Option 2): He is a physicist who served as the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, not a judge.

 

• Rajiv Ranjan (Option 4): Not a Chief Justice of India.

question: Identify the animal that is NOT a non-chordate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Repltiles.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The question asks for the animal that is NOT a non-chordate, i.e., the one that IS a chordate. Reptiles belong to the phylum Chordata (sub-phylum Vertebrata). (सरीसृप — कॉर्डेटा संघ)

 

• Chordates are animals possessing a notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord, and pharyngeal gill slits at some stage of their life; reptiles, being vertebrates, possess a vertebral column derived from the notochord.

 

• Examples of reptiles include snakes, lizards, turtles, and crocodiles — all classified under Class Reptilia within phylum Chordata.

 

• The other three options — Arthropods, Porifera, and Arachnids — are all invertebrate (non-chordate) phyla/groups lacking a notochord or vertebral column.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Porifera (sponges) are the simplest multicellular animals, with a cellular level of organisation and no true tissues.

 

• Arachnids (spiders, scorpions) are a class within phylum Arthropoda, characterised by eight legs and two body segments.

 

NOTE

 

• Arthropods (Option 2): This is a non-chordate invertebrate phylum, characterised by jointed appendages and an exoskeleton.

 

• Porifera (Option 3): This is a non-chordate invertebrate phylum (sponges), the simplest multicellular animals.

 

• Arachnids (Option 4): This is a non-chordate invertebrate class under Arthropoda, including spiders and scorpions.

question: Asiad is regulated by_________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Olympic Council of Asia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Asian Games (Asiad) are a multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from across Asia, regulated by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA). (एशियाई खेल — ओलंपिक परिषद एशिया)

 

• The OCA was founded in 1982, with its headquarters in Kuwait City, Kuwait, and is recognised by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) as the governing body for sport in Asia.

 

• The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi in 1951, and the event was formerly regulated by the Asian Games Federation before the OCA took over in 1982.

 

• The Asian Games are the second-largest multi-sport event in the world after the Olympic Games.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2023 (19th) Asian Games were held in Hangzhou, China.

 

• India's Olympic Association, the national body affiliated to the IOC and OCA, is called the Indian Olympic Association (IOA).

 

NOTE

 

• International Olympic Council (Option 1): No such body exists by this exact name; the global Olympic governing body is the International Olympic Committee (IOC).

 

• Commonwealth Games Federation (Option 2): This body regulates the Commonwealth Games, not the Asian Games.

 

• Indian Olympic Council (Option 3): India's Olympic body is called the Indian Olympic Association (IOA), and in any case it only governs Indian participation, not the Asian Games as a whole.

question: Dhuadhar falls originate from which of the following river?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Narmada.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Dhuandhar Falls ("smoke cascade", spelled "Dhuadhar" in the question) is a waterfall formed on the river Narmada, located near Bhedaghat in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh. (धुआंधार जलप्रपात — नर्मदा नदी)

 

• The falls are named "Dhuandhar" (meaning "smoke cascade") because the force of the water crashing down creates a mist that resembles smoke.

 

• The falls occur at the point where the Narmada river, after flowing through the famous Marble Rocks (Bhedaghat) gorge, narrows and plunges down.

 

• The Narmada river originates from Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh and flows westward into the Arabian Sea (Gulf of Khambhat), unlike most other Indian peninsular rivers which flow eastward.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Narmada also forms the traditional boundary between North India and South (Peninsular) India.

 

• Other notable Narmada river features include the Sardar Sarovar Dam in Gujarat.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahanadi (Option 1): This river flows through Chhattisgarh and Odisha, forming the Chitrakote Falls, not Dhuandhar.

 

• Godavari (Option 2): The largest peninsular river, flowing through Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh; not the source of Dhuandhar Falls.

 

• Krishna (Option 4): This river flows through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh; not the source of Dhuandhar Falls.

question: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court of India pronounce the theory of the ‘Basic Structure’ of the Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kesavananda Bharati Case, 1973.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The "Basic Structure" doctrine of the Constitution was propounded by the Supreme Court in the landmark Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) case. (केशवानंद भारती मामला — मूल ढांचा सिद्धांत)

 

• The 13-judge bench (the largest ever constituted by the Supreme Court) ruled that Parliament has wide powers to amend the Constitution under Article 368, but cannot alter its "basic structure" or fundamental framework.

 

• Elements later held to be part of the basic structure include supremacy of the Constitution, secularism, federalism, separation of powers, and judicial review, among others.

 

• The case overruled the earlier position taken in the Golaknath case (1967), which had held that Fundamental Rights could not be amended by Parliament at all.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Minerva Mills case (1980) further strengthened the basic structure doctrine, striking down clauses of the 42nd Amendment that sought to give unlimited amending power to Parliament.

 

• The doctrine acts as a crucial check on the unlimited amending power of Parliament under Article 368.

 

NOTE

 

• Golaknath Case, 1967 (Option 2): This case held that Fundamental Rights are beyond the amending power of Parliament, but it did not establish the basic structure doctrine.

 

• Minerva Mills Case, 1980 (Option 3): This case reinforced and applied the basic structure doctrine (established in Kesavananda Bharati) but was not the case that originally propounded it.

 

• Swarn Singh Case, 1989 (Option 4): Not a recognised leading constitutional case relevant to the basic structure doctrine.

question: The year whose prices are being used to calculate the real GDP is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is base year.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Real GDP is calculated using the prices of a fixed reference year, called the "base year", to eliminate the effect of price changes (inflation) over time. (आधार वर्ष — वास्तविक जीडीपी)

 

• By contrast, Nominal GDP is calculated using the current year's prevailing (market) prices.

 

• Using a constant base year allows for a more accurate comparison of the actual physical volume/quantity of goods and services produced across different years.

 

• India's current GDP base year is 2011-12, as recommended by the Central Statistics Office (CSO), now the National Statistical Office (NSO).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The GDP Deflator is the ratio of Nominal GDP to Real GDP, used to measure the level of price inflation in the economy.

 

• Before 2011-12, India's GDP base year was 2004-05.

 

NOTE

 

• Current year (Option 1): Prices of the current year are used for calculating Nominal GDP, not Real GDP.

 

• Constant year (Option 2): "Constant prices" is a related term describing real GDP's methodology, but the specific reference year used is technically called the "base year".

 

• Fiscal year (Option 4): This simply refers to the accounting/financial year (April-March in India), not the base year concept used in real GDP calculation.

question: Ajmer became the suba headquarters under the ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mughals.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the Mughal Empire, Ajmer was made the headquarters of a suba (province), one of the administrative provinces created as part of Akbar's reorganisation of the empire. (अजमेर सूबा — मुगल साम्राज्य)

 

• Emperor Akbar divided the Mughal Empire into 12 subas (later increased to 15), each headed by a Subedar (governor); Ajmer suba covered much of present-day Rajasthan.

 

• Ajmer held great religious and strategic importance for the Mughals due to the Dargah of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti, which several Mughal emperors, including Akbar, visited on pilgrimage.

 

• Each suba was further divided into sarkars and parganas as part of the Mughal revenue and administrative system.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Akbar's land revenue system, the Zabt/Dahsala system, was administered by Raja Todar Mal across these Mughal provinces.

 

• Other major Mughal subas included Agra, Delhi, Awadh, Bengal, Malwa, and Gujarat.

 

NOTE

 

• Pallavas (Option 1): A South Indian dynasty (Tamil region), unrelated to the Mughal administrative suba system.

 

• Cholas (Option 2): A South Indian dynasty known for its own administrative units (mandalams, valanadus), unrelated to Mughal subas.

 

• Delhi Sultanate (Option 4): The Delhi Sultanate used a different administrative division called "iqta", not "suba", which was a specifically Mughal term.

question: The headquarters of the National Institute of Oceanography of India is located at:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Goa.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Institute of Oceanography (NIO) has its headquarters at Dona Paula, Goa. (राष्ट्रीय समुद्र विज्ञान संस्थान — गोवा)

 

• NIO was established on 1 January 1966 as one of the constituent laboratories of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR).

 

• It conducts research on all aspects of oceanography, including physical, chemical, biological, and geological oceanography, along with ocean engineering and marine environmental studies.

 

• NIO also has regional centres located in Mumbai, Kochi, and Visakhapatnam.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), a different body focused on ocean engineering technology, is headquartered in Chennai.

 

• NIO operates research vessels for oceanographic surveys, coastal and deep-sea research in the Indian Ocean region.

 

NOTE

 

• New Delhi (Option 1): Not the location of NIO headquarters; it hosts many other central government bodies instead.

 

• Hyderabad (Option 2): Not the NIO headquarters; Hyderabad hosts other institutions like the National Remote Sensing Centre.

 

• Kanyakumari (Option 3): A coastal town but not the location of NIO's headquarters.

question: Unemployment arising due to mismatch between Job availability in the market and skills of available worker is called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Structural.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Structural unemployment occurs due to a mismatch between the skills possessed by workers and the skills demanded by available jobs in the market. (संरचनात्मक बेरोजगारी — कौशल असंतुलन)

 

• It typically arises from changes in the economy's structure, such as technological advancement, automation, or shifts in industry demand, that render certain worker skill-sets obsolete.

 

• It is considered a longer-term and more persistent type of unemployment compared to other types, as it usually requires retraining or skill development of the workforce to resolve.

 

• Structural unemployment is distinct from a simple shortage of jobs — the jobs may exist, but the available workers lack the relevant skills to fill them.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Frictional unemployment occurs due to the natural time lag involved when workers transition between jobs, even in a healthy economy.

 

• Cyclical unemployment arises due to the business cycle, increasing during economic recessions/downturns.

 

NOTE

 

• Seasonal (Option 1): This type of unemployment occurs due to seasonal fluctuations in demand for labour (e.g. agriculture, tourism), not a skills mismatch.

 

• Economical (Option 3): Not a standard, formally recognised category of unemployment in economics.

 

• Frictional (Option 4): This refers to short-term unemployment while workers search for or transition between jobs, not a skills mismatch.

question: Ravikirti was the court poet of which of the following dynasty ruler?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chalukyas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ravikirti was the court poet of the Chalukya ruler Pulakeshin II, and is famous for composing the Aihole Inscription (Prashasti). (रविकीर्ति — चालुक्य वंश)

 

• The Aihole Inscription, dated 634 CE, is written in Sanskrit in the Kannada script and is a key source of information about the reign and military conquests of Pulakeshin II, including his victory over Harshavardhana.

 

• Pulakeshin II was one of the greatest rulers of the Badami Chalukya dynasty, known for successfully repelling Harshavardhana's invasion on the banks of the river Narmada.

 

• Ravikirti described himself in the inscription as being equal in poetic skill to Kalidasa and Bharavi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Badami Chalukyas ruled from their capital at Vatapi (Badami) in present-day Karnataka.

 

• Other notable Chalukya-era rock-cut architecture is found at Badami, Aihole, and Pattadakal.

 

NOTE

 

• Cholas (Option 1): A Tamil dynasty of South India; their court poets are not linked to Ravikirti or the Aihole inscription.

 

• Cheras (Option 2): An ancient Tamil dynasty of Kerala/Tamil Nadu region, unrelated to Ravikirti.

 

• Pallavas (Option 3): A South Indian dynasty famous for Mahabalipuram's monuments; Ravikirti was not their court poet.

question: India’s First AI-powered, end-to-end digital Lok Adalat was launched in ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's first AI-powered, end-to-end digital Lok Adalat was launched in Rajasthan in August 2022. (डिजिटल लोक अदालत — राजस्थान)

 

• It was inaugurated jointly across Rajasthan and Maharashtra on 13 August 2022, but it was specifically credited as being launched/pioneered by Rajasthan, under the initiative of the Rajasthan State Legal Services Authority (RSLSA).

 

• The initiative used Artificial Intelligence to help identify, categorise, and match cases suitable for settlement through Lok Adalats, aiming to speed up dispute resolution and reduce the burden on courts.

 

• Lok Adalats are a form of Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) in India, organised under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, where pending or pre-litigation cases are settled amicably.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) is the apex statutory body constituted to provide free legal aid and organise Lok Adalats across India.

 

• The digital Lok Adalat model aimed to allow parties to participate remotely, improving access and reducing pendency of cases.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 1): Not the state credited with launching India's first AI-powered digital Lok Adalat.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): Not associated with this particular initiative.

 

• Gujarat (Option 4): Not associated with this particular initiative.

question: Kagyed dance, a customary dance festival which is celebrated annually in Sikkim falls in which month?
solution_text:
The correct answer is December.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kagyed dance (Kagyat Chaam) is a customary masked dance festival celebrated annually in Sikkim, typically falling in the month of December. (कग्येद नृत्य — सिक्किम, दिसंबर)

 

• It is performed on the 28th and 29th day of the 9th month of the Tibetan lunar calendar, which corresponds to December in the Gregorian calendar.

 

• The festival is performed by monks of the Nyingma sect of Tibetan Buddhism at monasteries such as Rumtek, Phodong, and Tsuklakhang, and involves masked ritual dances symbolising the destruction of evil spirits.

 

• Kagyed is performed two days before Losoong (the Sikkimese New Year), marking the culmination of the year with rituals to ward off evil for the coming new year.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Losoong, the Sikkimese New Year festival, is celebrated by the Bhutia community and closely follows the Kagyed festival.

 

• Other well-known Sikkim festivals include Saga Dawa and Pang Lhabsol.

 

NOTE

 

• May (Option 1): Not the month of Kagyed dance; Saga Dawa, another Buddhist festival, generally falls around May-June.

 

• October (Option 2): Not the month associated with the Kagyed dance festival.

 

• August (Option 4): Not the month associated with the Kagyed dance festival.
